title: Proportional reservation controller and attention pacing to reduce microburst tail latency
creator: Maya Patel
description: Background: We observe recurring microburst tail latency events when heterogeneous workloads (short chat prompts mixed with long attention-heavy prefill requests) coincide on GPUs. Existing admission and batch shaping heuristics sometimes overcommit kernels or create cache thrash, causing 99.9th latency regressions for interactive customers. This ticket implements a two-part approach: (1) a proportional reservation controller that computes lightweight fractional slot reservations per tenant/route based on recent observed throughput and tail risk, and (2) an attention pacing layer that defers and micro-slices prefill scheduling to avoid triggering expensive kernel transitions and KV cache churn. Goal is to reduce 99th/99.9th token latency by at least 30% for mixed workloads without lowering overall throughput by more than 5%.
design_notes: Reservation controller: maintain a per-tenant exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) of active prefill arrivals and successful completions over 60s; convert to a fractional slot quota with leaky-bucket smoothing and a configurable min-reservation floor.
Proportional admission: when queue depth spikes, admission selects requests weighted by reservation fraction, then by deadline (shortest remaining tokens) to reduce head-of-line blocking.

Attention pacing: identify attention-heavy requests using a cheap estimator (context_length * attention_cost_factor derived from model meta) and insert micro-slices (prefill sub-allocations) that allow sharing of kernels across concurrent decodes and avoid large KV cache evictions.
Kernel-aware hints: admission emits a kernel-hint tag (e.g., 'fused-attn' vs 'flash-attn') so the scheduler favors compatible co-located batches; this avoids repeated kernel swaps on the same GPU.

Safety: controller is conservative by default; initial alpha parameters to EWMA are tuned to avoid oscillation. Emergency fallback: global burst allowance token which bypasses reservations for a short period when SLOs are met.
Compatibility: works with existing shapers (batch-shaper) by exposing an adapter interface; does not require runtime changes to model execution path.
Observability: track reservation utilization, rejected-by-quota counts, micro-slice fragmentation, and per-kernel swap rate.
Tradeoffs: increased scheduling overhead (small) vs lower tail latency. Potential slight throughput loss for very bursty but homogeneous long-request workloads.
Security: no new surface; reservation state is ephemeral and per-tenant; no PII stored. Security review not required unless we add audit logging to reservations (see dependencies).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 wks): Implement EWMA-based reservation controller in admission service; add per-tenant state and config; unit tests for quota math and smoothing.
Phase 2 (2 wks): Add attention estimator and micro-slice orchestration in prefill coordinator; implement kernel-hint tags emitted to scheduler.
Phase 3 (1 wk): Integrate with batch-shaper adapter; e2e load tests on staging with mixed synthetic workloads; tune parameters.
Phase 4 (1 wk): Canary rollout on a small Dedicated pool with runtime-1.22; monitor metrics and rollback conditions.
Code locations: admission service (runtime/admission), prefill coordinator (runtime/prefill), scheduler adapter (runtime/scheduler/hints).
rollout_plan: Canary: 5% traffic to a dedicated pool in us-west with mixed synthetic traces for 48h.
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 60% over 72h with automated rollback if 99.9th token latency increases by >10% or throughput drops by >7%.
Full: enable by default for new deployments after 2 successful canaries and sign-off from SRE and PM.
Fallback: 'reservation=off' runtime flag and per-tenant opt-out for emergency rollbacks.
metrics: Primary: 99th and 99.9th token latency (prefill and decode) for mixed workloads.
Secondary: end-to-end throughput (tokens/sec), reservation utilization (%), kernel-swap-rate (swaps/min), micro-slice fragmentation (avg slices/request).
SLO thresholds for canary: 99.9th latency <= baseline*0.95 and throughput >= baseline*0.95.
Alerts: triggered if reservation rejection rate > 5% sustained for 10m or kernel-swap-rate increases by 2x.
Benchmarks: compare with existing adm-controller under standardized 70/30 short/long trace mix.
